title: amikor for a Whole Era, Not Just a Moment

sections.title: From "just then" to "back in that whole period"
sections.content: You already use *amikor* to catch one action interrupting another (*Sétáltunk, amikor elkezdett esni*). In a longer story it does more: an *amikor*-clause can set up an entire stretch of background time that the rest of the story happens inside, not just a single instant. Combine it with *akkoriban* or *korábban* to stretch the frame even further.

items.spanish: Amikor gyerek voltam, egy kis faluban laktunk.
items.english: When I was a child, we lived in a small village.

items.spanish: Amikor még Szegeden dolgoztam, akkoriban minden nap vonattal jártam be.
items.english: When I was still working in Szeged, back then I commuted by train every day.

items.spanish: Amikor a nagyapám fiatal volt, korábban egészen más volt itt az élet.
items.english: When my grandfather was young, life here used to be completely different.

sections.content: An *amikor*-clause that opens a story almost always pairs with *volt* or another descriptive past verb in the main clause, not an action verb — you're painting the setting, not moving the plot forward yet. Save action verbs (*történt*, *elindult*, *találkoztam*) for once the *amikor*-clause has done its job.
